title: ia read prints the body behind a locator; the runtime reads it with readBody
summary: The new ia read <locator> [--include-runtime] [--json] command in @inventarch/cli prints the body behind a locator with the SHA-256 of its UTF-8 bytes and the line "body not certified by this read". It opens the workspace without the db cache and writes nothing, and ia inspect keeps the record's structure. A locator is a canonical system/kind/facet/name identity; that identity with #<phase>/<Primitive> for the text of the record's cells at that address or #<REQ-ID> for one requirement's text; or <path>:<line> for the innermost admitted record whose source span holds that line. A cell or requirement locator reads that text, never a document. Otherwise a record whose word carries a source locator, and which states it, reads the document it names: work.source on `@spec`, `@plan` and `@task`, reference.document on `@authoring-guide` and template.resource on `@template`; a `@decision` or `@milestone` that states work.source reads its own body. The path is read relative to the tree holding the record's source: the workspace root for its own .ia/src, a package's or an installed store's directory, and for an adopted mount the directory .ia/workspace.json binds it to, whose documents the mount's revision pin does not cover. Files are read through the workspace file reader ia capture uses, which refuses a path through a link or junction, a missing, non-regular or hard-linked file, a name that is not portable and a file over 4 MiB; the bytes must be UTF-8. A source locator <path>#<anchor> on a .md or .markdown file, in any case, reads only the section from the ATX heading with that anchor to the next heading of the same or a higher level, headings in fenced code ignored. The anchor is GitHub's for a plain-text heading (repeated headings numbered -1, -2; a leading byte order mark is not part of the first heading); underscore emphasis, entity and character references, inline HTML and reference links are not rendered first, so such a heading may have another anchor on GitHub, and setext headings and headings in list items or block quotes are not read. Any other record reads its own body, its meaning.says (the head describes of a `@system`; a `@schema` has an empty body). With --json the result is {version, locator, identity, kind, path, digest, body, certified: false}, where kind is record or document and path is present for a document only. A malformed locator refuses with IA-CLI-USAGE (exit 2) before anything is read. The other refusals keep the runtime's codes and each names one next command: IA-RUNTIME-READ-UNADMITTED (exit 1: an identity is not in this workspace's sources and names the ia inspect overview, a line of a source whose records admission refused names ia validate, a line of an admitted source that no record spans names ia inspect --path, and a line of a file holding no record names the overview), IA-RUNTIME-READ-FRAGMENT (no such cell or requirement, exit 1), IA-RUNTIME-READ-UNREACHABLE (a document path that names no file or is outside the workspace or the record's tree, a file the reader refuses or cannot find, bytes that are not UTF-8, an anchor on a file that is not markdown or one no heading has; exit 3) and IA-RUNTIME-READ-PLACEMENT (a record at runtime placement, band 0, without --include-runtime; exit 3). The workspace session the CLI opens admits no source at runtime placement, so through ia read the flag changes nothing yet. @inventarch/runtime exports parseLocator, readBody(handle, locator, {read, mounts, includeRuntime}), fragmentText, markdownSection, headingAnchor, SOURCE_LOCATORS and READ_CODES with the Body, BodyResult, Locator, ReadBodyOptions, ReadCode and ReadRefusal types, and the @inventarch/runtime/internal/locator subpath. The host supplies read, the reader of one workspace file, and mounts, the directory of each adopted mount by the .ia/adopted/<id>/<revision> label its sources carry; the runtime reads no file itself, and without mounts an adopted record's document is unreachable. RUNTIME_CODES gains the four IA-RUNTIME-READ codes, so code that switches exhaustively over RuntimeCode must handle them. resolveMention checks a fragment with fragmentText and refuses exactly as before. @inventarch/db exports adoptedBindings(root), which returns the .ia/workspace.json bindings as frozen {id, path, revision, tree} values, validated as source discovery validates them but without reading or verifying the bound sources, with the AdoptedBinding type, and sourceTree(path), the tree a source path belongs to by the rule capture membership already applies. No Door operation reads a body, and MACHINE_PROTOCOL version 1, ia scope, workspace revisions and per-record digests are unchanged.
